title: Intent-Aware Caching for Efficient LLM Serving
summary: An intent-aware eviction policy for LLM prefix caches was evaluated on WildChat and ShareChat workloads. In the reported setup it achieved a 34.6% cache hit rate and reduced average serving latency by up to 46.1%; the workload patterns are observational and do not establish performance on other traffic.
ai_technology: Intent classifier and intent-aware cache eviction policy
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Analyses of WildChat and ShareChat traces found continuation probability and inter-turn delays differed by intent. Intent-aware caching reached 34.6% hit rate versus 18.8% for a prior learned approach and 12.2% for LRU, with latency reduction up to 46.1% in the reported evaluation.
evidence.unknown: Trace patterns are observational and depend on the learned intent taxonomy; effects outside the evaluated workloads and setups are unknown.
evidence.ai_role: An intent classifier labels requests; a learned eviction policy uses intent-conditioned reuse statistics to guide prefix-cache decisions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
